Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a direct disqualifier, not a tradeoff to re-litigate under urgency. The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly recovers both rather than just the downstream symptom. memory_86 supports shortening onboarding (completion + time-to-value) and memory_31 independently corroborates that reducing signup friction lifts SMB activation, which is the same mechanism from a different experiment; that convergence is why I favor onboarding over activation_messaging (memory_91), which addresses only the later stage. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does nothing for a top-of-funnel decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but misaligned with the SMB segment under attack.
